messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate on streaming/tool-call path for customer 'NimblePay' — >50% SSE disconnects, multiple parsing failures. Priority: P1. Paging oncall: @priya :rotating_light:

priya: picking this up. any customer-visible degradation besides disconnects?

alex: yes — we got 5 support tickets saying streaming responses stop mid-call. Some show `tool_call_parse_error` in logs.

maria: logs from gateway show a spike at 11:04:12 UTC: many `SSE client disconnected` with reason `read ECONNRESET`. Also a handful of `toolcall: parse failed: unexpected token` from the tool-runner.

sam: sending initial mitigation runbook — will scale dedicated streaming workers to soak. doing `kubectl scale deploy/stream-workers --replicas=12` now.

deploy-bot: Rollout started by sam — stream-workers -> 12 replicas.

priya: oncall handoff: I'm primary until 14:00 UTC. @alex you have logs + timeline; @maria you'll triage parsing boundary conditions. @cs-liaison please draft customer message if we confirm impact.

maria: sharing filtered logs (stack snippets):
```
[11:04:11.982] sse:conn=abc123 seq=0 client=10.2.14.8 - keepalive
[11:04:12.004] sse:conn=abc123 seq=1 payload=... - error EOF
[11:04:12.011] tool-runner: call_id=call-9a parse_error=UnexpectedToken at pos 234
[11:04:12.013] gateway: response_chunked client=10.2.14.8 size=0
```

maria: noticed the parse errors line up with `seq=1` reconnect attempts. hypothesis: reconnection + re-sent partial payload causes parser to see malformed JSON.

alex: also saw an increase in client reconnects from older SDK versions. user-agent strings: `nimble-sdk/1.3.2` vs normal `nimble-sdk/1.5.0`.

kieran: quick check — did we recently change SSE framing or any keepalive window? I don't see any recent deploys to streaming infra in the last 48h except small channel refactor a week ago.

sam: scaling done. traffic shifted, but disconnect rate only dropped from 52% -> 47%. not enough.

priya: customer impact: initial estimate ~12 customer sessions affected, 2 experienced tool-call failures leading to incomplete payments. CS wants proactive outreach if we can't fix in 2h.

cs-liaison: I can draft an acknowledgement note: short ETA + mitigating steps. Hold until we confirm root cause. :+1:

alex: digging into router traces — I can see duplicated POSTs from gateway to tool-runner for same call ID when client reconnects quickly. tool-runner cannot idempotently handle partial replays; it treats second chunk as new leading to parse error.

maria: reproducing locally: simulate client reconnect mid-stream, resend last chunk without `resume=true`, parser throws. adding small sample script: 
```
# simulate reconnect
curl -N -H "User-Agent: nimble-sdk/1.3.2" http://staging/stream -d '{"seq":0,"chunk":"hello"}'
# reconnect and resend partial
curl -N -H "User-Agent: nimble-sdk/1.3.2" http://staging/stream -d '{"seq":1,"chunk":""}\n'
```

kieran: ok that explains parse errors. two parallel mitigation tracks: 1) server-side quick fix to tolerate empty/resumed chunks (hotfix parser + guard), 2) client-side mitigations — ask customers to upgrade SDK to 1.5.0 where reconnects include `resume=true`.

sam: can we do server-side safe-guard quickly? maria, can you open a hotfix PR to guard on empty chunk and ignore until full payload assembled? label `hotfix/stream-parser`

maria: working on PR. simple guard: if chunk payload length == 0 && seq > 0 then buffer and wait 100ms for continuation instead of immediate parse. starting unit tests.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: hotfix/stream-parser -> canary to stream-workers (2 pods) once CI passes.

priya: timeline update for incident doc:
- 11:04 UTC - spike of SSE disconnects and parse errors observed
- 11:10 UTC - pager fired, oncall engaged
- 11:12 UTC - scaled stream-workers to 12 (temporary soak)
- 11:20 UTC - identified client versions / reconnect pattern
- 11:28 UTC - reproduced parsing failure locally
- 11:36 UTC - hotfix PR created by maria; canary deploy pending

alex: customer impact note for CS: "We're seeing intermittent streaming disconnects for older SDK versions that can cause tool call errors. We're rolling a hotfix and recommend upgrading SDK to 1.5.0. We'll follow up with timeline and remediation."

cs-liaison: sending to NimblePay: "We're investigating streaming disconnects causing partial tool-call failures. We're deploying a mitigation now and expect >60% reduction in errors within 15-30m. We'll update in 30m."

maria: CI green. deploying canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of hotfix/stream-parser to stream-workers-ccw-01 (2 pods) started by maria.

sam: watching metrics: error-rate local canary traffic drop from 51% -> 8% for canaried customers. looks promising.

priya: nice. roll to remaining workers if stable for 10m. Also create followup ticket to add idempotency keys on tool-runner and better resume semantics.

kieran: agreed — followup: make protocol explicit: reconnects must include resume flag or we must treat replays as idempotent. filing RFC-4667 to capture long-term change.

alex: also note: create server-side rate limiter for rapid reconnects per-client to avoid duplicate POST floods.

maria: rolling full rollout now.

deploy-bot: Rolling hotfix/stream-parser -> stream-workers (12 replicas) started.

sam: monitoring global error rate: from 47% -> 6% across affected customers after rollout.

priya: excellent. customer update: sending resolution note and offering assistance for SDK upgrade.

cs-liaison: sent. NimblePay replied: "Thanks — saw immediate improvement. We'll schedule SDK upgrade this week."

priya: incident status: mitigated. root cause: older SDKs reconnecting without resume semantics + parser not tolerant of empty/resumed chunks. action items:
- hotfix rolled out (maria, done)
- customer outreach (cs-liaison, done)
- followup RFC for resume semantics (kieran)
- durable fix: idempotent tool-runner and explicit resume header (engineering backlog)

alex: closing thread — I'll add logs/timeline to postmortem doc and assign owners on followups. thanks everyone. :tada:
